items.text: Climb plan: Masters 450 to Challenger

Coach mode: first principles, no win-rate data. Blunt on purpose.
Bronze to Masters 450 LP, one rank a season. Now low Diamond 4.
Written 2026-11-21, tab 7 added 2026-11-23. Tab 2 is arithmetic.
Start here: this is the one page to use. The rest of the Library is reference.
"Kog dies to assassins and can't play objectives."

You took him to Masters 450. The champion did not get
worse; your habits got rusty. Assassins kill the carry
who stands near fog without knowing where they are, and
that habit follows you to any champion. Objectives are
won by whoever arrives first with the wave pushed, not
by whoever has a dash.

"I'll keep playing Kog'Maw. I went 60% over 150
Masters games."

Good call. 60% is above Challenger pace (even its noise
range, about 52 to 68%, is above 50). The risk is your
pattern: you left Darius at 60% too, after losses to
matchups and teams. The champion was never the problem.
A loss you could not control is not evidence to switch.
"You can hit Challenger on any champ."

Agreed, and follow it through: then the champion is not
your bottleneck. You are the variable. Avoidable deaths,
tempo and mood decide your climb. Spend most of your
energy there, not on the champ list.

"I struggle to accept I can't have a 100% win
rate."

This is your biggest lever. Challenger pace is about
55%: you lose 9 of every 20. If a loss feels like
failure, you queue the next game to erase it, and that
is the game you throw. Grade each game on your
decisions, not the result.
"I climb one rank every season."

A steady learning rate, and it is real. But the decay
means you stopped playing. Challenger is a top-300
ladder that moves while you are away. It rewards a good
win rate held across hundreds of games, not one hot
month.
What separates Masters 450 from Challenger

Not mechanics. (1) Fewer avoidable deaths. (2) A plan
every minute: wave, recall, objective. (3) The same
quality in game 5 of a session as in game 1. All three
are habits you can train on purpose.
Games to climb 1,000 LP, by win rate

Assumes +20 / −20 LP. Low D4 to Masters 0 is ~400 LP;
the Challenger cutoff moves, so 1,000 is a round guess.
win rate
games
55%: 500 games
58%: 313 games
Twenty games at Challenger pace (55%) look like this:
Moss = win, red = loss. 11 wins, 9 losses, a 3-loss run in the middle. That is a great month.
What it says

• Win rate is a multiplier, not a detail. 52% needs
~1250 games, 55% ~500, 58% ~313. Every tilted game you
skip moves you right on this curve.
• Losses are built in. Even playing at a true 55%,
simulation says:
– 65% chance of a 5-loss streak somewhere in 100 games
– 25% chance you are under 50% after 20 games
– 20% chance you are still under 50% after 50
• So a losing streak is not proof you got worse, and a
short sample is not a verdict on a champion. Judge
yourself on decisions and deaths over 50+ games.
• The win you can control: the game you do not queue
while tilted. Skipping one coin-flip game you would play
at 40% is worth more than any build change.
Before you queue

Write one focus for the session, one sentence,
e.g. "Before I pass river, I say out loud where
their assassin is." 5 minutes of last-hitting in
Practice Tool. Mute all chat at load-in.
Play in blocks of 3

Three games, then stand up. Decide the next
block with a clear head, not in the queue pop.
Same hours each day if you can: consistency
beats marathons.
Stop rules (not optional)

Two losses in a row: done for the day. Typed
angry, or felt "I need this one back": done.
Last game of the day is never a loss you are
trying to erase.
One line after each game

Win or loss, did I keep my focus (yes / no), and
my one most avoidable death with its category
(below). Grade the game on that line, not on the
result.
Death review, twice a week

One loss and one win. Only watch the 10 seconds
before each of your deaths. Ask: what did I
know, what was I trying to do, what would a
Challenger player do here?
Weekly reset

Count avoidable deaths per game. Next week's
focus = the most common category. Watch 20
minutes of a Challenger player on your champ,
pausing to predict their next move before they
make it.
Death categories for the log
Unseen threat
Died to someone I had not tracked.
Greed

Stayed for a wave, plate or kill
past my safe line.
Bad fight

Took a fight my team loses on
paper.
Late

Arrived after them to an objective
and walked in.
Fair trade

Died for something worth more. Not
avoidable.
Target: halve the first four in a month. Masters players die to them every game; Challenger players rarely do.
The objective clock (Dragon, Grubs, Herald, Baron)
90 s before

Look at the waves near the pit.
Shove the lane on that side.
60 s before

Recall now if low or you can buy.
Never reset at 20 s.
30 s before

Arrive first, wave pushed,
wards down, stand behind them.
Spawn

The team that got there
first gets to choose.

Late or no prio? Do not face-check. Trade across the map:
tower plates, a tower, their camps. Losing a dragon is
cheaper than losing the carry and the dragon.
Count the missing

Glance at the map every wave. If two or more
enemies are missing, or their assassin is, you
farm the wave closest to your team or under
tower. No exceptions when you are the carry.
Their engage starts the fight

Hit whatever is in range, frontline included. Do
not walk forward to reach the backline until
their engage button is spent on someone else.
Then turn on.
Ahead: take buildings

A lead is gold you have not spent yet. Convert
it into plates, towers and objectives, not into
chasing kills into fog. A tower never flashes
back.
Behind: be the last one reachable

Farm safely, give up what you cannot contest,
let them overextend into your team. Every level
you reach alive moves the game toward a scaling
carry.
Every reset, three questions

What is the next objective and when? Which waves
crash where? What is my next item and can I
afford it? Leave base with the answers.
Judge the decision

A good call that loses to a coin flip is still a
good call. A bad call that works is still bad.
Log the call, not the outcome.
Phase 1 · D4 to Masters
Shake off the rust

• You were Masters 450; D4 is below your level. The
danger is impatience, not skill.
• Champion: Kog'Maw, locked. No new builds or runes
this phase.
• Focus: avoidable deaths ≤ 2 per game.
• Daily system from tab 3, stop rules strict.
• Exit: Masters.
Phase 2 · Masters to GM
Tempo

• Run the objective clock for every objective.
• Death review twice a week, weekly focus from the
log.
• Focus: arrive first, wave pushed, at most
objectives.
• Judge yourself over 50+ games, never over one
session.
• Exit: Grandmaster.
Phase 3 · GM to Challenger
Consistency and volume

• Your mechanics are already enough. Now it is about
the same level in every game.
• Track win rate by game number in a session. If game
4+ is worse, shorten sessions.
• Play steadily to the end of the season; the cutoff
rises late.
• Focus: no tilted games at all.
• Exit: top 300.
Your pace: 10 to 25 games a week

A standard week

• 10 to 25 games in blocks of 3, on 4 or 5 days. Same hours
each day.
• One death note after every game (tab 3): result, focus kept
or not, worst death and its category.
• Two VOD reviews, 25 minutes each (tab 6). Pick two set days
and keep them, even in a good week.
• Sunday: count avoidable deaths per game and set next week's
focus line.
• Stop rules still apply. A week of 10 calm games beats 25
with five tilted ones.
Honest expectation

Masters: 4 to 10 weeks at your 60% form, up to 20 at 55%.
Challenger: 10 to 25 weeks at 60%, 20 to 50 at 55%.

So aim for Masters, then GM, this season. Challenger this
season needs the top of your range and your 60% form held. It
is the same path either way. The 1,000 LP is a guess: check
the live cutoff.
Positioning checklist (say it in your head every fight)
Is W up?

W is on for 8 s of every 17. With it down you are a 500-range
champion: step back, do not show yourself until it is back.
Where are their gap closers?

Name each one out loud. Not on the map = assume it is in the
nearest fog to you.
Edge of W range, not past it

Hit the closest enemy at max range (630 to 710 with W). The
frontline is a fine target. Walking forward for the backline is
how you die.
Something between you and the fog

Your support, your frontline, a minion wave or a wall. Never be
the champion closest to the fog.
Know your exit first

Before the fight, know the step you take when they engage: toward
your team, never away into unwarded jungle.
Scout with R and wards, not your face

R gives sight and reveals for 2 s from 1,300+ range. Use it on a
brush before you walk past it.
VOD routine: 25 minutes, twice a week
Pick two games

One loss, one win, each with 2+ deaths. Never the same day you
lost it: review with a calm head.
Pass 1 · Deaths (10 min)

Jump to each death, rewind 15 s, pause. What did I know? What was
I trying to do? Log the category from tab 3.
Pass 2 · Fights (10 min)

Pause the moment the first enemy engages. Was W up? Was I at the
edge of W range? Who stood between me and them? Run the checklist
on the left.
Pass 3 · Objectives (5 min)

Pause 90, 60 and 30 s before each drake and Baron. Where was I,
and which waves were pushed?
Write one rule

Only one, e.g. "W down = I walk back." It becomes next week's
focus line before every queue.
The pattern to break

You went 60% on Darius and 60% on Kog'Maw, and both times
the urge was to swap after losses to matchups or teams.
Hunting for an 80% build is the same urge. No build gets
there: a Challenger player still loses about 2 in 5.
A loss you could not control goes in the log as "Fair
trade". It is not evidence. Only your decisions are.
Mechanics, 10 minutes before you queue

• Practice Tool: last-hit a wave under tower with W on.
• Kite the target dummy: attack, step back, attack. Never
stand still between autos.
• Land 10 R casts on a moving dummy, aiming where it will
be.
The build: locked until your 50 game review
AP (default)

Doran's Ring, Dusk and Dawn, then Rabadon's or Shadowflame,
Sorcerer's Shoes. Into squishy teams and short fights.
On-hit (into tanks)

Doran's Bow, Rageblade, then Terminus or BotRK. Into tanky teams
and long fights.
Runes (both builds)

Stormraider's Surge, Manaflow Band, Transcendence, Scorch. Second
tree: Legend: Alacrity, Coup de Grace.
Spells
Flash and Barrier.
Third item when they dive you
AP: Zhonya's or Banshee's. On-hit: Wit's End. No Quicksilver.
Behind into fed assassins
Stop feeding the lead

Each death is worth more to them than any farm is to you. Farm
with W and E from max range, give up a plate or a drake rather
than walk into fog.
Let them go first

Do not start the fight. Wait for their stun or engage to land on
someone else, then turn W on and shoot whoever came in.
Fight at chokes

Pits and warded jungle entrances make them walk to you. Open lanes
favour their flanks. If you cannot contest, take a tower on the
other side.
Ask for peel, use your E

Ping your support to stay with you, not roam. Your E slow is your
own peel: aim it at the gap closer, not for damage.

You 1v9 by being the last one they can reach: they spend their
buttons on your team, and you shoot for the 80 to 120 s after.
Why it is locked

Every build page in the Library ends the same way: the gaps
between builds are inside the noise.
A build change moves your win rate less than one game you
skip while tilted.
Change it only when Riot changes W's % health damage, Q's
attack speed or an AP ratio.
Where it comes from

• Items and keystone: "where Riot is taking him" (patch
26.22).
• Rune page: page A of "runes for aggression".
• Starters: the Doran's page. Spells: the spells page.
• Rules: "carry into fed assassins", tab 5.

source.basis: First principles and arithmetic, no win-rate data. Written as a coaching plan for Noah: Bronze to Masters 450 LP one rank per season (Darius top to D1, Kog'Maw ADC to Masters 450), decayed to low Diamond 4.
source.assumptions: Assumptions for the arithmetic only. Low D4 to Masters 0 is about 400 LP; the NA Challenger cutoff moves during the season and sits several hundred LP above Masters 0, so 1,000 LP total is a round illustration. Real gains depend on MMR.
source.simulation: Monte Carlo, 200,000 simulated runs of independent games at a true 55% win rate.
